subject: Private offer: staged prepay (3yr) — staircase discounts & true-up proposal
messages:
From: J. Singh <j.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer inquiry — 3yr prepay

Hi Avery,

We had a quick exec sync this morning and ACME is interested in pursuing a Marketplace Private Offer for Redwood. We are evaluating a 3-year committed prepay for inference credits (AWS Marketplace preferred).

High level asks:
- Significant term discount compared to on-demand — looking for guidance on realistic % for a 3-year commit.
- A staged ramp: Y1 expected consumption ~25% of commit, Y2 ~60%, Y3 ~100% — need protection on how unused prepaid credits are handled and any ramp credits.
- Billing cadence: prefer annual invoicing but open to discuss monthly true-ups.
- Need to understand SLA/financial remediation and how performance credits would be applied in a private offer context.

Can you share a starter term sheet and any Marketplace/offer mechanics we should be aware of? I can loop in legal/procurement once we have something to review.

Thanks,
Jai
Jai Singh
Head of Platform Engineering
ACME Corp

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: J. Singh <j.singh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — 3yr prepay

Jai — thanks for the clear summary. We can absolutely structure a Marketplace Private Offer on AWS that aligns with your ramp and annual prepay preferences.

Attaching a draft term sheet (RI_TermSheet_3yr_staircase_v2.docx) that outlines two recommended structures: a straight 3yr prepay (flat discount) and a staircase/staged prepay that gives a heavier discount on later-year committed volumes and explicit ramp protection (performance credits) if utilization lags.

Quick notes up front:
- Ballpark discounts: for a 3yr locked prepay we typically start conversations in the 18–30% range off list, but structure and payment cadence can move that. The staircase approach can push effective discounts higher in later years while protecting Redwood from decade-sized churn risk.
- Ramp protection: we offer a graded credit that returns a % of unused annual prepay as account credit if actual usage falls below agreed ramp thresholds. Credits are applied on annual true-up.
- Billing: we can do annual upfront invoices via AWS Private Offer (customer pays to AWS; AWS provides payout) — we can also support an annual invoice with quarterly usage reporting and a year-end true-up.
- Marketplace mechanics: AWS requires the private offer to specify contract term, pricing, and whether credits/refunds are supported; we can model the credit as an account credit applied by Redwood rather than a direct AWS rebate to keep marketplace flows simple.

I have cc'd Neha (sales lead on marketplace offers) and Marissa (finance lead) to scope the concession we can comfortably give. If you can share your detailed year-by-year expected usage (the SOW or spreadsheet), we will map specific numbers to the term sheet.

Next step: can you share the spreadsheet with the Y1/Y2/Y3 expected usage and your preferred cadence for invoicing?

Best,
Avery Johnson
Principal Sales Manager — Cloud & Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Avery — attaching our internal estimates (ACME_SOW_usage_estimates.xlsx). Key pieces:
- Target commit: $1.8M/year list (so $5.4M over 3 years if we pin to list).
- Expected consumption vs commit: Y1 25%, Y2 60%, Y3 100% (as noted). We want either: (a) a ramp credit that refunds unused Y1 as a % applied to future years, or (b) an agreed true-up with roll-forward credits applied to year-end invoice.
- We are sensitive to CPI/price escalation. If Redwood plans to increase list prices in later years, we need a floor/ceiling or CPI-link to avoid surprise increases.
- Termination: procurement will push for a limited termination-for-convenience in Y3 with a pro-rated refund for unwound committed spend.

Legal will want to see specific language around credits vs refunds and marketplace flow (AWS requires defined price and payment flow in the PO).

Thanks — sharing to legal/finance now.

Best,
Jai

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: J. Singh <j.singh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — Private Offer proposal & staircase mechanics

Jai — reviewed your spreadsheet. Below is a proposed structure designed to balance ACME's ramp risk with Redwood's ability to commit capacity and offer a compelling effective price.

Proposed commercial terms (summary):
- Contract: 3-year AWS Private Offer, prepaid annually (upfront to AWS via your procurement).
- Commit amount (example model): $1.8M/year list (we will model final price after you confirm target commitment).
- Discounting: Staircase % off list applied per-year on committed volume: Y1 = 18% off, Y2 = 24% off, Y3 = 30% off. Effective blended discount ~24% over 3 years under your expected ramp.
- Ramp protection / performance credits: If actual consumption in a year is below the agreed threshold (Y1 < 40% of year-1 commit, Y2 < 70% of year-2 commit), Redwood will issue account credits equal to 30% of the unused prepaid value for that year (credit applied to future Redwood invoices). Credits cannot be redeemed for cash from AWS — they will be Redwood account credits applied during private offer reconciliation.
- True-up mechanics: Quarterly usage reporting; annual reconciliation with credits/roll-forward. Unused credits at end of contract expire unless parties agree in writing.
- Price escalation: list pricing fixed for the 3-year term in the private offer. We will include a CPI cap for extraordinary macro moves — suggested language: list price increases limited to CPI + 2% per annum, capped at 5% total per year.
- Termination: No unilateral early cash refund in Y1–Y2. In Y3 Redwood will consider a termination for convenience with a 180-day notice and pro-rated credit for the remaining prepaid period less a 10% termination fee (subject to final approval).
- Marketplace notes: AWS private offer will show the contracted price and term. Because credits are handled by Redwood, the AWS PO will reflect the gross prepaid amount and Redwood will reconcile credits off-platform. This preserves AWS marketplace flows while giving ACME usable credits.

Attached: updated term sheet (RI_PrivateOffer_ACME_3yr_v1.pdf) with example numbers and a mock annual true-up worksheet.

If this looks directionally OK, I propose Redwood prepare a formal private offer and a redlineable Master Private Offer Addendum for ACME legal. Neha and Marissa — please confirm that finance is comfortable with the proposed credit structure and the termination concession.

Thanks,
Avery

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: J. Singh <j.singh@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer proposal & staircase mechanics — redlines

Avery — thanks for the proposal. Legal has a few redlines and clarifications before we can proceed to a formal PO: 

1) Ramp credits: request to increase application of unused Y1 value to 50% of unused prepay (instead of 30%) as a credit toward future invoices. 
2) Credit conversion: credits must be permitted to offset AWS Marketplace invoices or be distributable to ACME in the event of Redwood insolvency (we understand AWS constraints; if credits remain Redwood-account-only, require escrow language or covenant).
3) Termination in Y3: we request the termination-for-convenience with 120-day notice and pro-rated refund (no termination fee).
4) CPI / price lock: require a fixed list for first 2 years and CPI+1% cap in Y3 only.

Please confirm Redwood's comfort level with each point. For (2) legal will push to minimize operational risk related to credits sitting on Redwood's ledger.

We can accelerate if you provide a redlineable addendum; procurement will not sign a PO until legal confirms commercial mechanics.

Best regards,
Laura Chen
Senior Counsel — ACME Corp
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME private offer — decision points & recommended concessions

Team — summary and recommended path forward for ACME deal (deal_id ACME-2026-PO-17).

Key asks from ACME legal/procurement:
- Increase ramp credit from 30% -> 50% (ACME asks).
- Convert credits to be AWS-offsettable / require escrow protections.
- Shorten Y3 termination notice to 120 days and remove termination fee.
- Change CPI mechanics to fixed then CPI+1% in Y3.

Our recommended concessions (minimize cash exposure, keep marketplace flows intact):
1) Ramp credit — counter to 40% (compromise). Change credit to 40% of unused prepaid value in Y1/Y2 applied as Redwood account credit. Rationale: reduces immediate cash/regulatory exposure while offering stronger ramp protection.
2) Credit conversion / escrow — propose a custodian escrow: Redwood will segregate a % of gross prepaid funds (5% of annual prepay) into a custodian account held for the duration of the contract to provide additional recovery assurance. We will provide contractual covenant to prioritize ACME for Redwood account credits during insolvency proceedings up to the escrowed amount. This keeps AWS flows intact while addressing legal concern.
3) Termination — maintain 180-day notice and a modest 10% termination processing fee; offer to reduce fee to 5% if ACME increases the initial commit by 10%.
4) CPI — accept fixed list for first 2 years, CPI+1% cap in Y3.

Operational asks: finance needs a modeled cash-flow impact for the escrow and the 40% ramp credit. Marissa — can you run a model for (a) base term, (b) 40% credit, (c) 50% credit to quantify exposure and help price the termination fee concession?

If finance signs off, I will draft a redlineable Private Offer Addendum reflecting the above counters and send to ACME legal for their review. We should aim to get a signed private offer before end of September to hit Q4 revenue targets.

Thanks,
Avery
Principal Sales Manager — Cloud & Marketplace
Redwood Inference
